Experimental
A native Ala tRNA gives 100 units of charging; G3–C70 mutant gives 2; a non-Ala scaffold gives 1; that scaffold carrying G3·U70 gives 60. All RNAs have intact CCA. What is the strongest conclusion?

The determinant contributes to charging and is transferable in the tested scaffold|All tRNAs must carry G3·U70|The anticodon always defines amino acid identity|The mutation must eliminate all RNA folding
Loss in native RNA and gain in a recipient support a major identity determinant. The observations do not show universal sufficiency or prove complete unfolding.
Experimental
A minihelix lacking an anticodon is charged by AlaRS. Which conclusion is justified?
The minihelix can independently translate mRNA|An anticodon is not indispensable for charging that construct|All synthetases ignore anticodons|Ribosomes no longer need tRNA
The assay establishes charging of the reduced substrate, not decoding. It cannot generalize to every aaRS.
Experimental
A synthetase mutant retains ATP–PPi exchange but produces little charged RNA. Which next measurement best localizes the defect?
Total DNA concentration|Number of codons in the genome|Aminoacyl transfer and product hydrolysis separately|Number of ribosomal proteins
Activation appears possible. Direct transfer and stability assays distinguish deficient transfer from rapid loss of product.
Experimental
Wild-type enzyme hydrolyzes preformed Val-tRNA^Ile quickly; mutant and no-enzyme samples hydrolyze slowly. Correct Ile charging is similar for wild type and mutant. What is most supported?
A defect in transcription|A defect in codon pairing|Absence of CCA addition|A selective post-transfer editing defect
The substrate is already mischarged, so the experiment tests post-transfer hydrolysis. Correct synthesis is retained, narrowing the defect.
Numerical
A 240-residue protein is synthesized from standard directly charged tRNAs without futile cycles. What is the charging cost?
240 ATP molecules and 480 phosphate-bond equivalents|239 ATP and 478 equivalents|480 ATP molecules and 480 equivalents|240 GTP only
Every incorporated residue requires one charging event: 240 ATP → AMP, conventionally 480 equivalents. The 239 peptide bonds are not the charging count.
Numerical

A preparation releases 150 nmol AMP and accumulates 125 nmol correctly charged RNA. Assume each ATP-consuming attempt releases one AMP and no other AMP source or product loss. How many attempts did not yield correct accumulated product?
150 nmol|25 nmol|125 nmol|275 nmol
150−125=25 nmol. This discrepancy alone cannot distinguish editing stages or identify the wrong product.
Numerical
A hypothetical synthetase activates 990 correct and 10 wrong substrates. Editing removes 9 wrong products and no correct ones. What is the wrong fraction among surviving products?
Surviving products total 990+1=991. One is wrong. The denominator must exclude discarded products.
Numerical
Correct and wrong activation efficiencies are 500 and 5 M⁻¹ s⁻¹; the wrong amino acid is 20-fold more concentrated. Under low-substrate competition, what is the wrong activation fraction?
1%|20% exactly|50%|About 16.7%
Wrong/correct flux = (5/500)×20=0.2. Wrong fraction =0.2/1.2=1/6. The ratio is not the fraction.
Numerical
If 90% of ATP-consuming independent attempts yield correct product, what is the average phosphate-bond equivalent cost per correct product?
Mean attempts = 1/0.9; multiply by two equivalents per attempt. A fractional value is a population average.
Numerical
At 310 K, PPi activity falls 100-fold with all other activities fixed. How does the free-energy change of aminoacylation (before explicit PPi hydrolysis) shift?
+11.9 kJ/mol|−11.9 kJ/mol approximately|0|−100 kJ/mol
RT ln(0.01)=−2×8.314×310×ln(10) J/mol ≈ −11.87 kJ/mol. This is the shift, not the entire reaction ΔG.
Numerical
For a fixed RNA pool, k_ch=0.6 s⁻¹ and k_use=0.4 s⁻¹. If k_use doubles while k_ch remains fixed, what is the new steady-state charged fraction?
Use C/T=k_ch/(k_ch+k_use). The new utilization constant is 0.8 s⁻¹; the denominator is 1.4 s⁻¹.
Data interpretation
Acidic gel signals are 72 charged and 18 uncharged in sample A; 36 charged and 9 uncharged in B. Which inference is justified?
B has half the charged fraction|A has twice the charged fraction|B has completely inactive aaRS|Both have 80% charged, but B has half the total signal
72/90=36/45=0.8. Lower total signal could reflect abundance or technical recovery; fraction alone cannot identify flux.
Experimental
A mutant tRNA loses charging after a stem-disrupting substitution. A compensatory substitution restores base pairing but not the original sequence; charging returns. What is favored?
A structural contribution rather than strict requirement for original bases|Anticodon replacement is proved|ATP is unnecessary|The RNA must have acquired a new amino acid identity
Restoring pairing rescues activity despite changed sequence. This supports a structural requirement in the tested context, not universal absence of sequence-specific recognition.
Experimental
Two tRNAs bind a synthetase with similar apparent affinity; only one is aminoacylated efficiently. What explains the observation?
Binding always guarantees transfer|Productive positioning or chemistry may differ despite similar binding|Both must be charged identically|The result proves neither RNA binds
Association and catalysis are distinct. Bound substrate may be in a nonproductive orientation.
Experimental
An incorrect amino acid stimulates AMP release only when tRNA is present, but charged product is undetectable. What is the appropriate interpretation?
Pre-transfer editing is excluded|No ATP turnover occurred|Either tRNA-dependent pre-transfer or rapid post-transfer editing is possible|All amino acid was incorporated into protein
RNA binding can stimulate pre-transfer editing, while rapid post-transfer hydrolysis can conceal the intermediate. Separate assays are needed.
Integrative
A cell has normal total translation but elevated Val substitutions at Ile codons. Which direct observation distinguishes charging from decoding most effectively?
Normal mRNA abundance|Cell size|Number of tRNA genes|Detection of Val-tRNA^Ile before ribosome delivery
Direct detection of the wrong cargo on the Ile adaptor supports an upstream charging defect. Normal translation rate does not establish fidelity.
Experimental
An Ala tRNA anticodon is altered; G3·U70, CCA and fold remain intact. It is still charged with Ala. Which prediction is justified?
Its possible decoding targets change while charging identity can remain Ala|It must become charged with another amino acid|Its aminoacylation necessarily ceases|It can no longer interact with any RNA
An anticodon change can redirect pairing without changing recognition by AlaRS. Actual cellular incorporation depends on downstream compatibility and competition.
Multiple statements

An editing-defective mutant has normal cognate charging and weak wrong-product hydrolysis. I. Correct-only assay may look normal. II. Wrong-product accumulation may increase with a competitor. III. Every mutant protein must contain the same wrong residue. IV. The phenotype may depend on amino acid pools. Which are supported?
I and III only|I, II and IV|II and III only|All four
I, II and IV follow from selective loss of editing. III is false because errors are probabilistic and may affect multiple proteins and sites.
Integrative
An archaeon lacks GlnRS but contains a nondiscriminating GluRS and an active tRNA-dependent amidotransferase. What is the expected final product on tRNA^Gln?
Glu-tRNA^Gln always|Free glutamine only|Gln-tRNA^Gln after conversion|Gln-tRNA^Glu necessarily
Glu is attached first, then its side chain is amidated on tRNA^Gln. Lack of direct GlnRS need not prevent decoding glutamine codons.
Matching

Match observation 1. Exchange absent 2. Exchange retained, transfer poor 3. Preformed wrong ester hydrolysis lost 4. Correct charging but near-cognate codons misread with likely affected stage a. activation b. transfer/product stability c. post-transfer editing d. ribosomal decoding.
These observations localize likely defects to the relevant biochemical stage. Further assays are needed to establish the exact molecular lesion.
Data interpretation
At steady state, charging and consumption rate constants each fall fourfold while the total pool is unchanged. What happens in the simple first-order model?
Charged fraction stays the same but steady-state flux falls fourfold|Charged fraction rises fourfold|Both fraction and flux stay identical|All tRNA becomes uncharged
The ratio k_ch/(k_ch+k_use) is unchanged; flux k_use C is fourfold lower. Fraction and throughput are not interchangeable.
Numerical
A first selection produces wrong fraction p=0.04. Editing survival for wrong products is s=0.01 and for correct products c=0.90. What is the wrong fraction among released products?
Wrong survival is 0.04×0.01=0.0004. Correct survival is 0.96×0.90=0.864. Divide by their sum.
Experimental
A mutant protein hydrolyzes both correctly and incorrectly charged RNA ten times faster than wild type. What is the most plausible concern?
It is necessarily a superior editing enzyme|ATP is no longer needed|Loss of editing discrimination can waste useful product|Ribosomal decoding becomes error-free
Editing is useful only when incorrect cargo is preferentially removed. Excessive cognate hydrolysis may reduce usable charged RNA and increase futile cycles.
Integrative
During amino acid deprivation a bacterial strain accumulates uncharged tRNA and activates a RelA-dependent response. Which is the best interpretation?
Uncharged tRNA directly copies DNA|CCA addition synthesizes ATP|All peptide bonds are hydrolyzed by RelA|The charged state links nutrient supply to a translation-associated stress signal
Uncharged tRNA in an appropriate ribosomal context contributes to stringent-response signaling; it does not replace a synthetase or hydrolyze peptide chains.
Experimental

A cell-free reaction with Cys-tRNA chemically converted to Ala-tRNA^Cys incorporates alanine at positions selected by the Cys adaptor. Which control is most important for distinguishing adaptor-directed incorporation from ordinary Ala charging?

Establish that altered cargo remains attached and is not merely released and recharged onto Ala tRNA|Measure chromosome length|Remove all RNA from both reactions and expect normal synthesis|Determine the color of the solution

Free alanine could enter normal charging and obscure the inference. Tracking the adaptor-linked cargo distinguishes the two models; the experiment does not show all mischarged RNAs are accepted equally.
